claim: The Console Mobile Application supports several sign-in methods: root credentials, IAM user credentials, and federated login through IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS Single Sign-On), Microsoft Active Directory and third-party identity providers; AWS recommends IAM user credentials or a federated role.
question: FAQ: How do I sign in to the Console Mobile App?

values.display: owner/root credentials, IAM user credentials, and federated login
values.spoken: root, IAM user or federated sign in

values.display: We recommend using either IAM user credentials or a federated role to log in to the Console Mobile Application

evidence.quote: The Console Mobile Application supports several authentication methods, including owner/root credentials, IAM user credentials, and federated login via AWS Single Sign-On, Microsoft Active Directory and third-party identity providers.
We recommend using either IAM user credentials or a federated role to log in to the Console Mobile Application.

claim: If a mobile device is lost, an IAM user's credentials can be deactivated to prevent unauthorized access, but a root account cannot be deactivated.

values.spoken: a root account cannot be deactivated

values.display: an IAM user can be deactivated to prevent unauthorized access

evidence.quote: If you lose your device, an IAM user can be deactivated to prevent unauthorized access. Root accounts cannot be deactivated.

claim: The Console Mobile App supports MFA, and AWS recommends a hardware MFA device or a virtual MFA on a separate mobile device for the greatest level of account protection.
question: FAQ: Console Mobile App: Is MFA supported?

values.display: a hardware MFA device or a virtual MFA on a separate mobile device
values.spoken: yes, MFA is supported; use a hardware device or a virtual MFA on a separate phone

evidence.quote: Yes. We recommend using either a hardware MFA device or a virtual MFA on a separate mobile device for the greatest level of account protection.

claim: The Console Mobile App supports all FIDO certified hardware authenticators, such as YubiKey, for MFA, and software authenticators such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator and LastPass Authenticator.
question: FAQ: Which MFA authenticators does the Console Mobile App support?

values.spoken: any FIDO certified hardware key and common software authenticators

evidence.quote: The AWS Console Mobile App supports all FIDO certified hardware authenticators (E.g., YubiKey) for MFA.
The AWS Console Mobile App supports software authenticators such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, and LastPass Authenticator.

claim: In the Console Mobile App the only way to create resources is through AWS CloudShell with the AWS CLI; the app's graphical interface lets you view and sometimes modify resources, but not create them.
question: FAQ: Console Mobile App: Can I create resources?

values.display: the only way to create resources from the mobile app is to do so through the AWS CloudShell service using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI)
values.spoken: only through CloudShell and the CLI, not through the app's graphical interface

values.display: you cannot create resources through the graphical user interface

evidence.quote: Currently the only way to create resources from the mobile app is to do so through the AWS CloudShell service using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI). Otherwise, you can view and sometimes modify resources within the app's graphical user interface, however you cannot create resources through the graphical user interface.

claim: The Console Mobile App can generate a pre-signed URL for an S3 object; a pre-signed URL grants time-limited permission to download the object.

values.spoken: it makes a pre-signed URL for the object

values.display: A pre-signed URL grants time-limited permission to download the object

evidence.quote: You can use The Console Mobile Application to generate a pre-signed URL for an S3 object. A pre-signed URL grants time-limited permission to download the object.

claim: The Console Mobile App shows the CloudWatch custom dashboards your identity may access, but CloudWatch automatic dashboards are not yet supported in the app.

values.spoken: custom dashboards yes, automatic dashboards not yet

claim: You can view current usage charges in the Console Mobile App after enabling billing alerts in Billing Preferences, and your identity must have permission to view CloudWatch to see them.
question: FAQ: Console Mobile App: Can I view my current AWS usage charges?

values.display: you can view your current usage charges in the Console Mobile Application
values.spoken: yes, with CloudWatch permission and billing alerts enabled

values.display: your identity must have permission to view CloudWatch

evidence.quote: Yes, you can view your current usage charges in the Console Mobile Application. Simply visit your Billing Preferences page and select the checkbox to Receive Billing Alerts. In order to view usage charges, your identity must have permission to view CloudWatch.
